findings.reason: I confirmed that OptimizedCursorPaginator.get_item_key calls math.floor/ceil on the raw datetime field, and build_cursor always calls key(results[0]) when the cursor has no value, so any non-empty audit-log page with optimized_pagination=true raises TypeError; value_from_cursor also skips the datetime conversion that DateTimePaginator does.

Cursor.from_string accepts negative offsets, Django querysets reject negative slice indices, and paginate only catches BadPaginationError, so a cursor like 0:-5:0 gives a 500 rather than any "advanced" access, which shows the comments are wrong.

Line 71 runs on every request and dereferences organization_context.member, which is Optional; a non-superuser-flag caller without membership (e.g. a token or staff path) would crash the whole endpoint, and the raw is_superuser flag ignores active-superuser session semantics.
The comment claims a negative-offset optimization, but the code only clamps next-cursor offsets to 0 and prev cursors still pass through as before; this is a comment-accuracy issue only.

Grep confirms max_segment_spans is now only assigned and never read, the removed segment_span_count_exceeded metric/log has no replacement, and the Lua script hardcodes 1000 with silent zpopmin eviction.
Existing span-buf:s:* SET keys with a TTL of up to an hour would make ZADD, ZCARD, ZUNIONSTORE and ZSCAN fail with WRONGTYPE after the deploy, a real rollout hazard that the PR does not address.
ZUNIONSTORE defaults to SUM, so a payload present in both sets gets a doubled score and avoids eviction, but this needs duplicate payloads across subsegment keys, which is an edge case.
The redirect loop limit really was cut from 10000 to 1000 and the explanatory comment removed, a small undocumented behavior change for extremely deep trees.
The tests only add a constant end_timestamp_precise and none exercise the >1000-span eviction or ordering by timestamp, a real but ordinary test gap.
